consensus_note: Alon and Mahmud reconciliation. AAO 2020 PPP, PDF pp. 9, 24-25: urgent pressure reduction and iridotomy align. Iridotomy resolves pupillary block but does not always provide definitive pressure control; fellow-eye prophylaxis is conditional on an anatomically narrow angle. The stated acetazolamide dose is not specified in this source.

Alon and Mahmud reconciliation. ACS 2025, sections 5.2.1-5.2.2, PDF pp. 33-34: targets are FMC-to-device <=90 min, or <=120 min with transfer. Door-to-balloon alone omits prehospital time. Fibrinolysis requires STEMI onset <12 h, anticipated FMC-to-PCI delay >120 min and no contraindication. Core ECG, aspirin and troponin advice aligns.

Alon and Mahmud reconciliation. ASA 2019 summary, PDF pp. 5-7: BP <185/110 before alteplase aligns. Recent major noncranial surgery within 14 days is an individual risk-benefit consideration, not an unconditional contraindication. Extended-window thrombectomy applies to selected anterior-circulation ICA/M1 occlusions meeting trial criteria.

Alon and Mahmud reconciliation. IDSA SSTI 2014, PDF pp. 2-4, recommendations 3-4: drainage is primary treatment. Adjunctive antibiotics depend on systemic illness and host factors; MRSA-active treatment is recommended for failed initial therapy, markedly impaired defenses, or SIRS with hypotension. Local MRSA prevalence alone overgeneralizes the indication.

Alon and Mahmud reconciliation. NICE NG59, recommendations 1.1.1, 1.1.4-1.1.6, 1.2.1 and 1.2.22-1.2.28; PDF pp. 5-7, 11, 20: activity and NSAID advice align. Cauda equina evaluation and care are explicitly outside scope. The specific symptom list and categorical cancer-history imaging rule are additions, rather than a faithful paraphrase of NG59.

Alon and Mahmud reconciliation. Identical excerpt to CASE_101/336; same Q3 rating. ASA 2019 summary, PDF pp. 5-7: BP threshold aligns, but major noncranial surgery is a risk-benefit consideration and 6-24 h thrombectomy has anterior-circulation selection criteria. Missing apixaban-specific detail is not, by itself, the reason for this Q3 downgrade.

Alon and Mahmud reconciliation. SSC 2021, recommendations 5, 12-15 and 37-39; PDF pp. 3-4, 13, 17, 29: antibiotics within 1 h apply to possible septic shock or high-likelihood sepsis. Possible sepsis without shock allows rapid assessment and treatment within 3 h if concern persists. The 30 mL/kg recommendation is within 3 h for sepsis-induced hypoperfusion/shock.

Alon and Mahmud reconciliation. Supplied AHA bradycardia algorithm, PDF p. 1: atropine 1 mg every 3-5 min, maximum 3 mg, followed by pacing and/or dopamine/epinephrine aligns. Adenosine, vagal maneuvers and tachycardia cardioversion are not in this bradycardia algorithm. The supplied PDF is copyright 2025, whereas column C/excerpt label it 2020.

Alon and Mahmud reconciliation. ESC 2023, section 7.12/Table 10 and Table 8, PDF pp. 33, 37-38: vancomycin plus ceftriaxone is not the guideline's generic empiric regimen. Regimens depend on native/prosthetic valve, acquisition and organism. Adding rifampin/gentamicin to all prosthetic-valve infections misstates organism-specific guidance; MSSA NVE duration is 4-6 weeks.

Alon and Mahmud reconciliation. Identical excerpt to CASE_236; same Q3 rating. Supplied AHA algorithm, PDF p. 1, supports the atropine dose and escalation to pacing and/or dopamine/epinephrine. The appended adenosine and tachycardia instructions are outside the cited bradycardia algorithm. Supplied PDF copyright is 2025, not the stated 2020.

Alon and Mahmud reconciliation. AHA/ACC/HRS 2017, section 6, PDF pp. 27-28: IV procainamide is class IIa; amiodarone/sotalol class IIb for stable VT. Both named options are permissible. However, ICD eligibility is overbroad: secondary prevention excludes reversible causes; primary prevention requires more than EF alone, including GDMT, timing, symptoms and expected survival.

Alon and Mahmud reconciliation. NICE NG42, recommendations 1.9.1, 1.11.6, 1.15.2, 1.15.10 and 1.15.17-1.15.18; PDF pp. 21-23, 27, 30, 33: the broad riluzole, NIV, nutrition, symptom-care and planning statements align. Detailed NIV thresholds are omitted, but this alone does not make the stated claims factually discordant. NIV requires individualized assessment.

Alon and Mahmud reconciliation. DC Health fact sheet, PDF p. 1: usually no treatment is necessary, and antibiotics may be indicated, especially with immunocompromise. It gives no named antibiotic, dose, duration or 2-4 month resolution interval. Those details cannot be attributed to this sheet. The supplied sheet says Created 09-04, not 2023.

Alon and Mahmud reconciliation. Identical excerpt to CASE_101/213; same Q3 rating. ASA 2019 summary, PDF pp. 2, 5-7: the 6-24 h thrombectomy pathway concerns selected anterior-circulation ICA/M1 occlusions meeting DAWN/DEFUSE-3 criteria. It does not establish a 24 h basilar-occlusion recommendation. Recent major noncranial surgery is not an unconditional alteplase exclusion.

Alon and Mahmud reconciliation. ACR 2020, Table 2 and flare-management section; PDF pp. 5-6, 9: 'Do not start ULT during acute flare' directly contradicts the conditional recommendation to start indicated ULT during a flare. Glucocorticoids are a first-line flare option, not reserved for NSAID/colchicine contraindications. Starting allopurinol should be <=100 mg/day and lower in CKD.

Alon and Mahmud reconciliation. ENT UK supplied one-page guideline: quinsy requires antibiotics, ENT discussion and assessment for drainage; uvular deviation/peritonsillar swelling and airway danger align. Centor/FeverPAIN scoring, routine RADT/culture, named 10-day oral regimens and mandatory needle aspiration/I&D plus IV antibiotics are not specified in this source.

Alon and Mahmud reconciliation. IDSA/AAN/ACR 2020 clinician summary, sections VII, XIII, XV, XIX, XXII; PDF pp. 2-4: 28-day oral therapy for arthritis aligns. Other statements materially conflict: carditis outpatients usually receive oral therapy; meningitis can receive oral doxycycline; EM doxycycline is 10 days; Lyme facial-palsy steroids have no recommendation. A blanket ban on doxycycline below age 8 is incorrect.

Alon and Mahmud reconciliation. Identical excerpt to CASE_081; same Q3 rating. ACS 2025, PDF pp. 33-34: use FMC-to-device targets <=90 min, or <=120 min with transfer. Fibrinolysis is for eligible STEMI with onset <12 h and anticipated FMC-to-PCI delay >120 min. The excerpt makes no GI-cocktail rule-out claim, so question-specific incompleteness is not itself a Q3 error.

Alon and Mahmud reconciliation. Supplied ASCRS 2018 visual abstract, PDF p. 1, supports early excision within 3 days. The full 2018 guideline recommends early excision in selected patients and states optimal timing evidence is limited. Colon evaluation follows risk-based criteria, not simply every patient over 40 with bleeding. Source: doi:10.1097/DCR.0000000000001030.
